newsitem.title: USA: United Auto to buy 9 dealerships for $53 mln.
newsitem.headline: United Auto to buy 9 dealerships for $53 mln.

text.p: United Auto Group Inc on Tuesday said it definitively agreed to acquire nine automotive dealerships in the South and New York metropolitan area which represent the Chrysler, Infiniti, Lexus, Nissan and Toyota brands.

The automotive retailer agreed to pay about $53.0 million, including about $25.0 million in cash, promissory notes totaling $25.0 million and about $3.0 million in United Auto common stock. United Auto agreed to make certain additional payments contingent upon the future performance of the dealerships.

The company also agreed to make an additional cash payment to the extent that the common stock issued in the transaction is valued at less than $3.0 million when the shares become freely tradable. The transaction is expected to close by May 1, 1997, and is subject to manufacturer approvals as well as other customary conditions.
The dealerships, which had estimated 1996 revenues of about $430.0 million, are owned by John Staluppi and John Staluppi Jr.

The dealerships include southern dealerships located in West Palm Beach, Florida: Florida Chrysler-Plymouth Jeep Eagle; Palm Beach Toyota; Palm Infiniti and Palm Nissan, and New York metropolitan area dealerships, located on Long Island: Amity Toyota Superstore, Lexus of Massepequa, Westbury Nissan Superstore and Westbury Toyota. All of the dealerships also sell previously-owned vehicles and offer a complete range of services including service and parts, and the placement of financing and insurance.
